title: Attn fusion regression hunt and microbench
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the investigation notes for the latency regression we started seeing in late Jan 2025 when enabling the new fused QKV+Attention kernel (experimental toggle: runtime.attn.fused_qkv=true). The regression shows up most clearly for long sequences (seq_len >= 1024) and small batch sizes (B=1,2). The goal here is to document reproducible microbenchmarks, hypothesis, profiling artifacts, and a short action plan for a follow-up patch/rollback decision.

Observations (high-level):
- Baseline (pre-fuse) = existing path that runs separate q/k/v matmuls -> FlashAttention v1 kernel -> post-proj. Latency for seq=1024, B=1, model dim=2048, top_preset runs: ~172 ms per forward (A100 80GB).
- Fuse-on (new fused QKV+attn kernel) = single fused kernel that does qkv projection + attn compute in one pass. Measured ~199 ms for same config (approx +15.7% latency).
- Regression primarily affects seq_len >= 1024. For seq_len <= 512 difference is within noise (±3%).
- Throughput (tokens/s) dropped correspondingly; peak GPU SM utilization drops by ~8% when fused kernel is used on these shapes.

Hardware / env used for repro:
- GPU: NVIDIA A100 80GB (driver 535.x), CUDA 12.1
- Docker image: registry.redwood/runtime:ci-20250210 (triton + runtime patches applied)
- Triton / kernels: triton v2.1 patched locally (branch: triton/paged-attn-tiling-experiments)
- Benchmark harness: infra/bench/attn_microbench.py (attached in linked PR)
- Model shape: d_model=2048, num_heads=32, head_dim=64, seq_len variable

Repro commands (quick):
- baseline run:
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infra/bench/attn_microbench.py --seq 1024 --batch 1 --mode baseline --repeat 200
- fused run:
  RUNTIME_FLAGS="attn_fused=1" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python infra/bench/attn_microbench.py --seq 1024 --batch 1 --mode fused --repeat 200

Raw timings (median over 200 iters):
- seq=512, B=1: baseline=89.2 ms, fused=91.1 ms
- seq=1024, B=1: baseline=171.9 ms, fused=199.0 ms
- seq=2048, B=1: baseline=402.6 ms, fused=537.3 ms (worst-case regression grows with seq)

Profiling notes (what we ran and key files):
- Nsight Systems timeline captures (nsys) for both runs: attached to PR-3421 (artifact: nsys_fused_1024.qdrep, nsys_base_1024.qdrep). Timeline shows fused kernel has longer single-kernel duration and increased global memory traffic bursts.
- nvprof / CUPTI counters: L2 read/write increases ~22% on fused run for seq=1024. DRAM throughput peaks approx 12% higher and sustained longer.
- NVTX annotated flamegraphs: fused kernel contains both projection and attention loops, but warp occupancy is slightly lower (active warps per SM down ~6%).
- Cutlass/cublas offloads: baseline uses cublas GEMM for q/k/v projections (separate small GEMMs); fused kernel replaces those with custom triton kernels that do projection in shared memory then proceed to attn compute. We observed increased shared memory spills for head_dim=64 in fused path.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Memory-bound working set increase: By combining projection + attn we change data access patterns so that KV cache pressure and L2/Dram traffic increases for long sequences. Paged attention memory layout interacts poorly with fused kernel's tiling, causing extra loads.
2) Tile size / register pressure: fused kernel's tile choice (tile_m=128, tile_n=64) causes higher register usage -> lower occupancy on A100, impacting throughput on large seq.
3) L1/Shared memory thrashing for head_dim=64: combined code spills into local memory under some launch configs. Baseline relies on cublas optimized GEMMs which have well-tuned caching.
4) Paged-attn + fused kernel interaction: When paged attention runtime is enabled (runtime.attn.paged=true), fused kernel's streaming/prefetch assumptions break and cause repeated page fetches.

Experiments run so far (and quick results):
- Change tile sizes in fused kernel (tile_m=64, tile_n=128) -> slight improvement for seq=1024 (~-3% latency) but increased for seq=2048 (+6%). Suggests tiling sensitivity.
- Force use of L2 caching hints (cudaFuncSetAttribute) -> no meaningful diff.
- Disable paged-attn while fused kernel on -> regression disappears (fused run w/o paged = baseline-ish). This is a strong signal that paged-attn + fused path is main interaction.
- Run with reduced head_dim (32) -> fused path now faster than baseline (~-8%). So regression is head_dim dependent.

Important trace excerpt (annotated):
- baseline: q_proj (cublasGEMM) 1.8 ms -> k_proj 1.8 ms -> v_proj 1.8 ms -> flash_attn kernel 162 ms -> out_proj 2.5 ms
- fused: fused_qkv_attn kernel 198 ms -> out_proj 2.6 ms
- Note: fused kernel contains multiple internal phases but shows a single long GPU kernel in timeline (harder to overlap with other async copies).

Why this might not have been caught earlier:
- CI microbench uses seq_len up to 512, and majority of customer workloads are <=512. The performance cliff only manifests for longer context workloads (LLM agents, long-document search).
- Our internal presets for PR performance gating don't include paged-attn enabled + fused toggle combination.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Roll back toggle runtime.attn.fused_qkv to false for 2025-02 canary release.
- Keep fused kernel in code but gate-on head_dim <= 48 or disable when paged-attn enabled. (safer short-term fix)
- Add a shape-specific heuristics table in runtime that picks kernel variant (baseline vs fused) considering seq_len, batch, head_dim, paged-attn flag.

Next experiments to do (actionable):
- A1: Reproduce with H100 (different SM count/register file) to see if regression persists on newer architecture. (owner: Ethan)
- A2: Add NVTX within fused kernel to break out projection vs attention phases to verify where the memory spikes happen. (owner: Asha)
- A3: Run microbench with artificial pinned memory pressure to emulate paged-attn page faults and confirm hypothesis about page-induced re-fetch. (owner: Miguel)
- A4: Implement a fallback: when paged-attn=true and seq_len>1024 and head_dim>=64 prefer baseline path. Add unit test and perf gating. (owner: Lena)

Open questions / discussion points:
- Is the fused kernel implementation using the most recent Triton auto-scheduler heuristics? (cc @infra/release)
- Can we get a quick review from low-level kernels team about register pressure vs. tile sizing tradeoffs? (cc @applied-ml/kernels)
- If we implement shape heuristics, what's the right policy surface to expose to customers (auto only vs explicit toggle)?

Short-term decision recommendation (team consensus):
- For the Feb canary we should disable fused_qkv when paged-attn is enabled (fast rollback path) and merge a shape-heuristics feature flag by EOD 2025-02-21. This avoids surprising regressions for long-context customers while keeping fused path on for shorter contexts where it helps.

Notes / rough todo list:
- [ ] Draft PR that gates fused path based on paged-attn flag and seq_len threshold (PR template: perf/regress-hotfix). (Lena)
- [ ] Share nsys captures and nvprof counters in PR artifacts (Ethan)
- [ ] Add CI microbench shape for seq_len 1024 with paged-attn enabled to catch future regressions (Asha)
- [ ] Schedule 30m sync with kernels team to review tile/register tradeoffs (Miguel)

Raw experiment outputs and logs are attached in the linked PR and in internal s3 bucket: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/attn-fuse-regress/ (index file inside PR).

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing locally
- pull runtime branch: git fetch origin && git checkout pr/attn-fuse-3421
- build container: docker build -t runtime:attn-fuse -f docker/Dockerfile.runtime .
- run microbench (see commands above). If you need the full harness, see infra/bench/README.md.

If you have extra time before the sync, please try H100 repro or run the fused kernel with head_dim=32/48 and seq_len 1024 to see cross-arch behavior.

References / useful links:
- PR with fused kernel impl: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3421
- CI perf graph comparison (internal): https://perf.redwood/inference/attn_kernel/compare/3421-vs-main
- Previous notes on paged-attn layout: confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Paged-Attention-Layout-Notes

Status: Draft. Will update after A1-A3 experiments complete and we have nsys captures on H100.

-- Lena (notes taken during ad-hoc profiling session, 2025-02-12 to 2025-02-20)
